# Charness v8.15.0

## What changed

- `charness task run` no longer stops a lane on a wall clock by default. A progress rule bounds every lane instead. A window of `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECONDS` (default `1200` seconds; `0` turns the rule off, and a negative value falls back to the default) can pass with no new commit, no file change, and no new command result. When that happens, charness interrupts the executor and resumes its session with a checkpoint request: commit what is coherent and report, reply `BLOCKED:`, or keep going. If the next window also shows no progress, charness stops the lane itself (`NO-PROGRESS-STOP:`). No human or orchestrator has to watch for the stop to happen. A test, lint, or typecheck command rerun with the same text on an unchanged tree is not progress. On its 3rd run the lane is asked to switch to the debug skill, on its 4th to checkpoint, and on its 5th the lane is stopped. The window check never kills a command younger than one window, but a loop message or stop does not wait for a running command. A command still running a window later can be killed, so set the window above the longest command a lane legitimately runs. Codex resume after this kill was probed live. Muse resume after a kill was not probed. `--timeout-seconds` still works as an explicit hard cap, but it no longer has a default. For the final attempt, `progress_guard.progress_rule` in the task result records each window check, rule message, and rule stop, and `execution.preemptions` counts preemptions when there were some. `task status` shows the live window state.
- Executor lanes that `charness task run` launches now have network access inside their workspace-write sandbox. Codex lanes get `-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` and Muse lanes get `--sandbox-network enabled`. Before this, the lane sandbox refused tests that bind a local port or fetch through the proxy, with `listen EPERM` or a proxy `502` response. The release tests check the flags the carrier passes, not a bind or fetch inside a sandbox. The read-only reviewers (self-review and the brief critique) drop that setting, so their sandbox is unchanged.
- `charness task run` now stamps each JSON-object line of a lane's `<executor>.events.log` with `charness_received_at`, the UTC time the carrier received that line from the executor's pipe. Before this, Codex items and Muse envelopes carried no wall time, so a lane could not say how long a command or phase took. Non-JSON lines are unchanged, and so are the rest of each event's bytes.
- `charness task status <task-id> --commands` reads that stamped log back and reports the lane's longest commands, how many commands it started in each family (test, lint, typecheck, merge), and its time per phase. The option is refused without a task id. Durations are receive-time estimates. Pipe buffering can delay either end of a command, so a duration can differ from the executor's own timing in either direction. A stamp without a timezone counts as unstamped. A lane run before this release has an unstamped events log, so for that lane the report counts command starts but gives no durations or phase times.
- Stamping never loses event bytes silently between the executor's pipe and the lane log. Every byte the executor writes before its pipe closes reaches the lane's stdout log, on normal exit, timeout, interrupt, and preemption, and a Codex lane then appends that log unchanged to `codex.events.log`. Charness adds only the stamp field on JSON lines and a newline after an unterminated final line. Some loss can still happen: a descendant process may keep the pipe open past the process-group kill, or a log write may fail or accept only part of a line. Either case is recorded in the task result as `execution.event_capture_incomplete`. After a log write fails, the reader keeps draining the pipe, so the executor does not block on a full pipe. A log write that hangs instead of failing can still stall the pipe. A Muse lane copies only a bounded tail of its stdout log into `muse.events.log` and skips an invocation that emitted no Muse event; that copy is outside this guarantee.
- The debug skill names a follow-up record after the branch that writes it. Before this, every follow-up was named by counting the files in its own worktree, so parallel lanes picked the same number and their merges collided. When the skill can read the checked-out branch from the git files and it is not `main`, `master`, `trunk`, or `develop`, a follow-up record's name ends in `-followup-<slug>-<hash>.md` (with the default title, `<date>-debug-review-followup-<slug>-<hash>.md`), and a further follow-up from the same branch on the same day adds a `-2` suffix. `<slug>` is the lane id for a `task/<lane>` branch and the branch name otherwise, as a lowercase slug (`branch` when nothing survives), and `<hash>` is a short hash of the full branch name. Records from different branches of that kind differ unless their hashes share a prefix. On a default branch, a detached HEAD, or branch metadata the skill cannot read, the old counter remains, so worktrees there can still pick the same name. The `latest.md` pointer works as before, so parallel lanes that each write a follow-up can still both change `latest.md`.

## Update

Run `charness update`, then run `charness version` to confirm the installed version. No migration is required. A launcher that passes `--timeout-seconds` keeps that hard cap until it drops the flag. To rely on the progress rule alone, drop the flag. Set `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECONDS` above the longest command your lanes legitimately run if that exceeds the default. `--no-progress-seconds` is still the separate first-edit budget for require-change lanes, not the progress window. Lanes now have network access, and this release has no per-lane switch to turn it off.

# Agent task runs

> Status: current
> Source of truth: this page and the `charness task run/status` implementation
> Last verified: 2026-10-17

`charness task run` executes one bounded lane; `task status` reads its external
result store. There is no scheduler lifecycle. `--executor` defaults to
`codex` (`gpt-6-luna`, effort medium/xhigh/max); `muse` uses its default model
and effort medium/high/xhigh/max.

The receipt's canonical executor block is `payload["executor"]`. Codex keeps
legacy aliases and log names; Muse records its trusted lane worktree as the
workspace because its runner has one effective workspace, not Codex's
`--add-dir` grants. Readers should branch on `executor.kind`. Executor names
the agent runner (`codex`/`muse`); carrier names where the candidate lives
(`carrier_kind`: `commit-only`, `commit-plus-dirty`, `worktree-only`,
`unknown`), not who ran it.

`--require-change` shapes implementation prompts and records edit/test phases. A scope mismatch retains a typed blocker rather than silently selecting a substitute owner.

The [progress rule](../charness-artifacts/spec/lane-progress-rule.md), not a wall clock, bounds a lane: a `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECONDS` window (default 1200) without commits, file changes, or new command results resumes the executor with a checkpoint request; a second stops it. `--timeout-seconds` is an optional cap.

`--report-only` inspects without changing and never reports a writer conflict.
Interrupted work with a proven empty scope is `interrupted-before-edit`; WIP is
reserved for changed work whose completeness is unknown. A useful dirty
candidate can be retained for review even when blockers deny approval.

Terminal receipts carry `result_kind` and a stable blocker. The CLI exit-code
mapping is owned by `charness task run --help`.
Transient stream stalls retry in the same worktree (three attempts by default,
30-second backoff), recording each failure kind. Finished-but-unapprovable
work needs review, merge, or re-scope; it does not need relaunch. Scope closure
stays warning-only (#831), a typed scope mismatch records a
`scope_extension_request`, and refresh excludes lane-created directories.
Secret-pattern environment names are scrubbed except
executor auth keeps and `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_KEEP_SECRET_ENV`; the receipt records
names, never values.

## Learning and resumed orchestration

Task-run friction events use WI-1 event-schema v1 and live in
`task-run/friction-log.jsonl` under the external task runtime root. A second
same-kind event from a distinct task run within 30 days carries
`repair the pattern, don't reshape the command`; nothing repairs it
automatically. Writer
conflicts are recorded for operator resolution.

`charness task report [--window 30m]` renders the fixed-shape period report
from lane metrics, the friction log, and the decision ledger: goals, lane
states, friction with repairs, measured improvements with the period
`improvements found:` line, decisions plus what needs the operator, and the
next-action table. Every section carries measured numbers, not prose claims.

Keep the active principles, DAG file, and handoff in the parent repo's
`.charness/task-run/orchestration-pointers.md`; every newly built lane prompt
reads it when nonempty, so a resumed orchestrator restores those pointers at
its next launch (the builder does not detect host compaction).

## Run

```bash
charness task run \
  --repo-root . \
  --lane feature-lane \
  --scope src/example.py \
  --prompt "Implement the requested slice and run its focused tests" \
  --effort xhigh
```

A clean parent is required. Model/effort identity, scope expansion, candidate
carrier, `changed_line_gate`, and retention live in
[`task_run_contract.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_contract.py),
[`task_run_scope.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_scope.py),
[`task_run_git.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_git.py),
[`task_run_changed_line.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_changed_line.py),
[`task_run_completion.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_completion.py),
[`task_run_retention.py`](../scripts/task_run/task_run_retention.py), and
[`runtime_root_retention.py`](../scripts/gates_support/runtime_root_retention.py).
Do not recopy receipt fields here; `--help` is the typed surface. `--scope`
repeats; `--skip-prepare` and `--allow-no-change` are diagnostic opt-outs;
`--path` and `--branch` are for exceptional host setup; `--base` also
overrides the lane HEAD base in shorthand.

The parent reads the receipt before integrating. A lane is done only when
`changed_line_gate` is `clean` or `noop`. Useful dirty work is committed before
proof; completion re-observes after the gate and denies approval for dirt, read
failure, or changed identity. Retention releases a finished worktree only when
the lane-branch commit carries the whole candidate (`commit-only`, clean tree)
with a `clean`/`noop` changed-line proof — even when other blockers deny
approval. Anything else (dirty tree, missing proof, persistence or observation
failure) keeps `keep_worktree` true. That flag is a newest-N hold, not a pin:
the sweep keeps the newest 10 kept worktrees per key with their `runtime/` dirs
and removes older ones only after verified salvage; `result.json` and logs
always stay. Writes block only when committed or dirty parent paths intersect actual
candidate paths; missing candidate evidence refuses completion. Declared
scope is advisory.

## Detach and wait

```bash
charness task run --repo-root . --lane x --detach
charness task wait --repo-root . <task-id>... [--any]
```

`--detach` returns once the carrier has started (exit 0 with the task id
and result path) or with the launch failure's exit code; `--dry-run` reports
the scope refusal with the launch's own code instead of launching. `task
wait` blocks until the named lanes end and exits with the finished lane's
code, so a host background job's notification carries the verdict.
`--rules-file` names standing material by absolute path (never inlined,
never scope evidence); `--grant-writable` grants a codex lane one
host-state directory (refused for muse, the repo root, `$HOME`, and `/`).

## Status

```bash
charness task status --repo-root .
charness task status --repo-root . <task-id>
```

Status reads the external result store. Each record adds read-time `liveness`
(`runner_pid` and advisory `alive`); a dead pid on a `running` record is stale,
while a live pid on a terminal record is normal during retention.

Each JSON line of `<executor>.events.log` gains `charness_received_at` (UTC
pipe receive time); `task status <task-id> --commands` reports command
durations (receive-time estimates), family starts, and phase times
([owner](../scripts/task_run/task_run_event_timing.py)). Event bytes lost at
close land in `execution.event_capture_incomplete`.

### Aggregate running-task inventory

`charness task status --repo-root <parent> --all-repos` returns the running count across immediate sibling keys in the caller's managed runtime tree, without task-ID prefix filtering or recursive scans. The [runtime owner](../scripts/runtime_bootstrap.py) and [retention owner](../scripts/gates_support/runtime_root_retention.py) derive that boundary. A standalone runtime root reports its narrower scope; neither claims whole-machine coverage.

Only canonical `task-run/*/result.json` records count. Live running records count as running, dead running records as stale, and known terminal states as terminal even while their runner finishes retention. Unknown status, unreadable or malformed storage, and unconfirmed liveness make completeness partial. Status never repairs records. An admission caller must consume both `completeness` and `running_count`; successful query execution is not admission approval.

Complete schema-bearing JSON/YAML delivery is exposed as `result_delivery.structured`;
review-lifecycle input is also projected as `reviewer_lifecycle`. Bounded review
JSON stays reusable as `reviewer_result`, including partial, deferred, blocked,
timed-out, or failed runs, but is not approval until a consumer rebinds its
packet, input identity, and task receipt. Malformed review JSON is retained as
partial-schema for retry; prose is not applicable. Terminal records and bounded
logs remain available in the external result store.

"""The lane progress rule: the one stop condition a task-run lane has.

A wall-clock timeout killed productive lanes mid-edit and let a looping lane
burn its whole budget. This rule replaces it with progress. Progress since the
last check is any of: a new commit, a file change, or a new command outcome
(a completed command whose (command text, worktree fingerprint) pair this lane
has not completed before; rerunning a command on an unchanged tree is not
new). Every progress window the rule checks. A window without progress earns
a checkpoint request; a second one in a row, with the request unanswered,
stops the lane. A hung command, a silent model and a dead executor are the
same case, so there is no second timer.

Loops are judged at each command completion: the third completion of the
same test, lint or typecheck command on an unchanged worktree asks the lane
to switch to the debug skill, the fourth asks it to checkpoint and stop, and
the fifth stops it.

The rule is pure over its inputs: the clock is the caller's `now`, the
worktree is read through an injected fingerprint, and an unobservable
worktree (`None`) counts as progress, so the rule never stops a lane it
cannot see. The watch (`task_run_progress`) applies its actions.
"""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Action:
    """What the watch must do now: send `message` (preempting) or `stop`."""

    kind: str
    text: str
    reason_code: str


def worktree_fingerprint(worktree: Path) -> str | None:
    """One hash of HEAD, the tracked diff, and untracked files, or None if unobservable.

    Ignored files (build output, caches) do not count. Untracked files are
    read by size and modification time, not content, so a rewrite counts as a
    change; the error is toward progress, never toward a false stop.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for args in (
        ("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
        ("diff", "HEAD", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-color", "--binary"),
        ("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z"),
    ):
        try:
            result = run_process(
                ["git", *args], cwd=worktree, timeout_seconds=_FINGERPRINT_PROBE_SECONDS
            )
        except OSError:
            return None
        if result.returncode != 0:
            return None
        digest.update(result.stdout.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape") + b"\0")
        if args[0] == "ls-files":
            for name in sorted(filter(None, result.stdout.split("\0"))):
                try:
                    stat = os.stat(worktree / name, follow_symlinks=False)
                except OSError:
                    continue
                digest.update(f"{name}\0{stat.st_size}\0{stat.st_mtime_ns}\0".encode(
                    "utf-8", "surrogateescape"
                ))
    return digest.hexdigest()

    check; delivery waits for its completion or the next check), and
    `delivered` (the next empty check stops the lane).

        self,
        *,
        window_seconds: float,
        fingerprint: Callable[[], str | None],
        window_source: str = "default",
    ) -> None:
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        self.window_source = window_source
        self._fingerprint = fingerprint
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._timeline = _timing._Timeline(on_complete=self._on_complete)
        self._muse_kinds: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._outcomes: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
        self._pending: Action | None = None
        self._last_check_at: float | None = None
        self._last_state: str | None = None
        self._last_progress_at: float | None = None
        self._new_outcomes = 0
        self._request: str | None = None
        self._in_flight_at_check: set[str] = set()
        self._invocation = 0
        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.stop_reason: str | None = None

    def start(self, now: float) -> None:
        """Begin observing at `now`; a later call starts the next invocation.

        Window state carries over a preemption; command state does not: the
        previous executor process is dead, and a resumed Codex session reuses
        item ids, so each invocation gets a fresh timeline and its own keys.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self._last_check_at is None:
                self._last_check_at = now
                self._last_progress_at = now
                self._last_state = self._fingerprint()
            else:
                self._invocation += 1
                self._timeline = _timing._Timeline(on_complete=self._on_complete)
                self._muse_kinds = {}

    def _in_flight(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {
            f"{self._invocation}:{key}": command
            for key, command in self._timeline.in_flight().items()
        }

    def on_event(self, event: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Action | None:
        with self._lock:
            if self.stop_reason is not None or self.window_seconds <= 0:
                return None  # stopped, or the rule is off: no message reaches the lane
            self._count_edit_outcome(event)
            self._timeline.feed(None, event)
            action, self._pending = self._pending, None
            return self._record(action)

    def _count_edit_outcome(self, event: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        """File edits the executor reports are outcomes even when git cannot be read."""
        item = event.get("item")
        if (
            event.get("type") == "item.completed"
            and isinstance(item, Mapping)
            and item.get("type") == "file_change"
        ):
            self._new_outcomes += 1
            return
        payload = event.get("payload")
        if not isinstance(payload, Mapping):
            return
        task_id = str(payload.get("task_id"))
        inner = payload.get("event")
        if event.get("payload_type") == "task.lifecycle.proposed" and isinstance(inner, Mapping):
            self._muse_kinds[task_id] = str(inner.get("task_kind") or "")
        elif event.get("payload_type") == "task.lifecycle.completed":
            kind = self._muse_kinds.get(task_id, "")
            if kind.startswith("tool.") and kind != "tool.bash":
                self._new_outcomes += 1

    def _on_complete(self, command: str | None, exit_code: object) -> None:
        if not command:
            self._new_outcomes += 1  # an unnamed command cannot be proven a repeat
            return
        state = self._fingerprint()
        # An unreadable tree is one unknown state: a new command is still new,
        # a rerun is not, and no loop is claimed without seeing the tree.
        key = (command.strip(), state or "unobservable")
        count = self._outcomes.get(key, 0) + 1
        self._outcomes[key] = count
        if count == 1:
            self._new_outcomes += 1
        if state is None:
            return
        if count > 1 and self._request == "deferred" and not self._in_flight():
            # The deferred request waited for this boundary, and the command
            # produced nothing new: deliver it now.
            self._request = "delivered"
            self._pending = self._checkpoint_request(interrupted=None)
            return
        if count < 3 or not LOOP_FAMILIES & set(_timing.command_families(command)):
            return
        shown = command.strip()[:200]
        if count == 3:
            ending = f" (last exit code {exit_code})" if isinstance(exit_code, int) else ""
            self._pending = Action(
                "message",
                LOOP_DEBUG_REQUEST.format(command=shown, count=count, exit=ending),
                "loop-debug",
            )
        elif count == 4:
            self._pending = Action(
                "message",
                LOOP_CHECKPOINT_REQUEST.format(command=shown, count=count),
                "loop-checkpoint",
            )
        elif count == 5:
            self._pending = Action(
                "stop",
                f"loop: `{shown}` completed {count} times on an unchanged worktree; "
                "the debug and checkpoint requests went unanswered",
                "loop-stop",
            )

    def _checkpoint_request(self, *, interrupted: str | None) -> Action:
        text = CHECKPOINT_REQUEST.format(window=_duration(self.window_seconds))
        if interrupted:
            text += (
                f" Your running command `{interrupted[:200]}` was interrupted after "
                f"running for at least {_duration(self.window_seconds)}; it may have "
                "left partial output or files. Do not simply rerun it: run a narrower "
                "or faster variant, or report that it needs longer."
            )
        return Action("message", text, "no-progress")

    def on_tick(self, now: float) -> Action | None:
        with self._lock:
            if self.window_seconds <= 0 or self._last_check_at is None:
                return None
            if now - self._last_check_at < self.window_seconds:
                return None
            state = self._fingerprint()
            tree_changed = state is not None and state != self._last_state
            progressed = tree_changed or self._new_outcomes > 0
            in_flight = self._in_flight()
            young = set(in_flight) - self._in_flight_at_check
            self._in_flight_at_check = set(in_flight)
            check = {
                "elapsed_s": round(now - self._last_check_at, 3),
                "progress": progressed,
                "new_outcomes": self._new_outcomes,
                "tree_changed": tree_changed,
                "tree_observable": state is not None,
                "commands_in_flight": len(in_flight),
                "commands_started_since_check": len(young),
                "request_before": self._request,
            }
            self.checks.append(check)
            self._last_check_at = now
            self._last_state = state if state is not None else self._last_state
            self._new_outcomes = 0
            if progressed:
                self._last_progress_at = now
                if self._request == "delivered":
                    self._mark_answered(True, "progress")
                self._request = None
                return None
            if young:
                # A command started after the last check has run less than one
                # window, and preemption never kills a command that young: the
                # request (or stop) waits for its completion or the next check.
                check["deferred_for_young_command"] = True
                if self._request is None:
                    self._request = "deferred"
                return None
            if self._request in (None, "deferred"):
                self._request = "delivered"
                interrupted = list(in_flight.values())[-1] if in_flight else None
                return self._record(self._checkpoint_request(interrupted=interrupted))
            self._mark_answered(False, "unanswered")
            window = _duration(self.window_seconds)
            return self._record(
                Action(
                    "stop",
                    f"no commit, file change, or new command result in two consecutive "
                    f"{window} windows; the checkpoint request went unanswered",
                    "no-progress-stop",
                )
            )

    def _mark_answered(self, answered: bool, by: str) -> None:
        for message in reversed(self.messages):
            if message["reason_code"] == "no-progress":
                if "answered" not in message:
                    message.update(answered=answered, answered_by=by)
                return

    def finish(self, *, ended_normally: bool) -> None:
        """The executor stopped running; a clean end answers a delivered request.

        A clean end is the executor's own exit 0 (its final report or a
        `BLOCKED:` line ends the turn); a timeout, interruption, or failure
        leaves the request unanswered.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self._request == "delivered":
                if ended_normally:
                    self._mark_answered(True, "lane-ended")
                else:
                    self._mark_answered(False, "lane-failed")
            self._request = None

    def _record(self, action: Action | None) -> Action | None:
        if action is None:
            return None
        if action.kind == "stop":
            self.stop_reason = action.text
        else:
            self.messages.append({"reason_code": action.reason_code, "text": action.text})
        return action

    def snapshot(self, now: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self._lock:
            since = None if self._last_progress_at is None else now - self._last_progress_at
            return {
                "window_seconds": self.window_seconds,
                "seconds_since_progress_seen": (
                    None if since is None else round(max(0.0, since), 3)
                ),
                "checkpoint_request": self._request,
            }

    def receipt(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self._lock:
            return {
                "window_seconds": self.window_seconds,
                "window_source": self.window_source,
                "stop_enabled": self.window_seconds > 0,
                "checks": list(self.checks),
                "messages": [dict(message) for message in self.messages],
                "stop_reason": self.stop_reason,
            }

def _resolve_lane_executable(
    value: str, *, empty_error: str, not_runnable: str, not_on_path: str
) -> str:
    """The one executable-resolution core; wrappers only name their executor."""
    if not value.strip():
        raise TaskRunError(empty_error)
    if "/" in value:
        candidate = Path(value).expanduser().resolve()
        if not candidate.is_file() or not os.access(candidate, os.X_OK):
            raise TaskRunError(f"{not_runnable}: {value}")
        return str(candidate)
    resolved = shutil.which(value)
    if resolved is None:
        raise TaskRunError(f"{not_on_path}: {value}")
    return resolved


def _resolve_codex(value: str) -> str:
    return _resolve_lane_executable(
        value,
        empty_error="--codex must name an executable",
        not_runnable="Codex executable is not runnable",
        not_on_path="Codex executable is not on PATH",
    )


def resolve_executor_executable(value: str, *, executor: str) -> str:

        not_runnable=f"{executor} executable is not runnable",

def validate_lane_id(lane: str) -> str:
    """Validate the safe identifier used by shorthand lane mode."""
    value = lane.strip()
    if not _TASK_ID_RE.fullmatch(value):
        raise TaskRunError(
            "--lane must be a non-empty id starting with a letter or digit and "
            "containing only letters, digits, dot, underscore, or dash (maximum 96 characters)"
        )
    return value


def _task_id(branch: str, requested: str | None) -> str:
    if requested is not None:
        task_id = requested.strip()
        if not _TASK_ID_RE.fullmatch(task_id):
            raise TaskRunError(
                "--task-id must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, "
                "digits, dot, underscore, or dash (maximum 96 characters)"
            )
        return task_id
    slug = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", branch.replace("/", "-")).strip("-")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(branch.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"{slug[:87] or 'task'}-{digest}"


#: Network for executor lanes (operator, 2026-10-20). Codex: the
#: workspace-write sandbox's own network switch. Muse: `--sandbox-network`
#: (`restricted|enabled|proxy-only`, default proxy-only).
CODEX_LANE_NETWORK_CONFIG = "sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true"
MUSE_LANE_SANDBOX_NETWORK = "enabled"


def build_codex_args(
    *,
    effort: str,
    writable_dirs: Sequence[Path] = (),
) -> list[str]:
    """Build Codex host arguments with the task runner's fixed Luna model."""
    # Lanes run loopback servers and fetches in their tests; the operator allowed
    # network for task-run lanes (2026-10-20). Lane worktrees carry no credentials.
    # The key configures only workspace-write; the read-only reviewers (self-review,
    # brief critique) drop it with `read_only_codex` so their argv is unchanged. It
    # follows `-m` with the other `-c` overrides, so a steer resume moves it
    # into the `exec resume` parser scope with them (see ef7c520ed).
    args: list[str] = ["--sandbox", "workspace-write"]
    for writable_dir in writable_dirs:
        args.extend(["--add-dir", str(writable_dir.resolve())])
    args.extend(["-m", TASK_MODEL])
    if effort not in TASK_EFFORTS:
        allowed = ", ".join(TASK_EFFORTS)
        raise TaskRunError(f"--effort must be one of: {allowed} (codex executor)")
    args.extend(["-c", f"model_reasoning_effort={effort}", "-c", CODEX_LANE_NETWORK_CONFIG])
    return args


def read_only_codex(command: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Turn a lane's Codex argv into a read-only reviewer's: no write, no lane network."""
    command[command.index("--sandbox") + 1] = "read-only"
    for index in range(len(command) - 1):
        if command[index] == "-c" and command[index + 1] == CODEX_LANE_NETWORK_CONFIG:
            del command[index : index + 2]
            break
    return command


def build_codex_command(
    executable: str,
    *,
    effort: str,
    writable_dirs: Sequence[Path] = (),
) -> list[str]:
    """Build the Codex command; the task prompt is supplied on stdin."""
    return [
        executable,
        "exec",
        *build_codex_args(effort=effort, writable_dirs=writable_dirs),
        "-",
    ]


def build_muse_args(
    *,
    effort: str,
    prompt_file: Path,
    worktree: Path,
) -> list[str]:
    """Build Muse host arguments with the task runner's curated effort preset.

    `muse exec` takes no stdin prompt, so the lane prompt travels via
    `--prompt-file`. Approval prompts cannot be answered headless, so they are
    disabled; the OS sandbox stays on (the Codex lane's workspace-write
    equivalent) with its network enabled like the Codex lane's. `muse exec` honors a single effective workspace (the last
    `--workspace` wins), so the lane worktree root is passed exactly once:
    passing every writable dir rooted the lane at `<worktree>/.agents` and
    every write outside it was refused (#814). The lane worktree is created
    for the agent, so it is trusted: otherwise the repo's rules are skipped
    and delegation stays unavailable. `--json` streams machine-readable
    events on stdout: without it the lane stdout stays empty until the run
    ends, so a timed-out lane receipted no phases and no retry cause (#886).
    The terminal report is extracted from the `run_terminal` event, separate
    from that JSONL transport.
    """
    if effort not in TASK_MUSE_EFFORTS:
        allowed = ", ".join(TASK_MUSE_EFFORTS)
        raise TaskRunError(f"--effort must be one of: {allowed} (muse executor)")
    return [
        "--json",
        "--reasoning-effort",
        effort,
        "--disable-approval",
        "--sandbox-network",
        MUSE_LANE_SANDBOX_NETWORK,
        "--trust-workspace",
        "--workspace",
        str(worktree),
        "--prompt-file",
        str(prompt_file),
    ]


def build_muse_command(
    executable: str,
    *,
    effort: str,
    prompt_file: Path,
    worktree: Path,
) -> list[str]:
    """Build the Muse command; the task prompt travels via --prompt-file."""
    return [
        executable,
        "exec",
        *build_muse_args(
            effort=effort, prompt_file=prompt_file, worktree=worktree
        ),
    ]


#: Env-name fragments (case-insensitive) treated as secret-bearing (#832).
#: The lane child inherits ambient env, and an executor may re-emit its
#: environment where any local process can read it (observed: muse
#: `--env-json` argv). Names only are ever matched or recorded, never values.
_SECRET_ENV_FRAGMENTS = (
    "API_KEY",
    "APIKEY",
    "_TOKEN",
    "TOKEN_",
    "SECRET",
    "PASSWD",
    "PASSWORD",
    "PRIVATE_KEY",
    "CREDENTIALS",
    "ACCESS_TOKEN",
    "AUTH_TOKEN",
    "REFRESH_TOKEN",
    "SESSION_TOKEN",
    "CLIENT_SECRET",
)
_SECRET_ENV_EXACT = frozenset({"TOKEN", "API_KEY", "SECRET", "PASSWORD"})

#: Executor auth keys that must stay in the lane env to function (#832).
#: Muse authenticates from its stored credentials; codex reads its key here.
_EXECUTOR_SECRET_KEEPS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    "codex": frozenset({"OPENAI_API_KEY"}),
    "muse": frozenset(),
}

#: Operator override: comma-separated exact env names to keep in lane env.
LANE_KEEP_SECRET_ENV = "CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_KEEP_SECRET_ENV"


def _is_secret_env_name(name: str) -> bool:
    upper = name.upper()
    return upper in _SECRET_ENV_EXACT or any(
        fragment in upper for fragment in _SECRET_ENV_FRAGMENTS
    )


def scrubbed_lane_env(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    env: Mapping[str, str],
    executor: str,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Drop secret-pattern names from the lane child env, recording names (#832).

    Unknown executors keep nothing secret-patterned (fail closed). Only the
    executor's auth keeps and explicit `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_KEEP_SECRET_ENV`
    names survive; the receipt records scrubbed/kept names, never values.
    """
    keeps = set(_EXECUTOR_SECRET_KEEPS.get(executor, frozenset()))
    for extra in os.environ.get(LANE_KEEP_SECRET_ENV, "").split(","):
        if extra.strip():
            keeps.add(extra.strip())
    scrubbed = sorted(
        name for name in env if _is_secret_env_name(name) and name not in keeps
    )
    kept = sorted(
        name for name in env if _is_secret_env_name(name) and name in keeps
    )
    payload["lane_env"] = {
        "executor": executor,
        "scrubbed": scrubbed,
        "kept_secret_names": kept,
    }
    return {name: value for name, value in env.items() if name not in scrubbed}


def task_runtime_root(repo_root: Path) -> Path:
    """Resolve the result store by clean parent identity, ignoring ambient roots."""
    preview_env = os.environ.copy()
    for key in ("CHARNESS_RUNTIME_ROOT", "CHARNESS_RUNTIME_ROOT_AUTO", "CHARNESS_RUNTIME_REPO_KEY"):
        preview_env.pop(key, None)
    return runtime_root(repo_root, preview_env)


def task_result_path(runtime_path: Path, task_id: str) -> Path:
    if not _TASK_ID_RE.fullmatch(task_id):
        raise TaskRunError(f"invalid task id: {task_id!r}")
    return runtime_path / "task-run" / task_id / "result.json"


def task_execution_runtime_root(runtime_path: Path, task_id: str) -> Path:
    """Return the lane-private runtime root beneath one task result directory."""
    return task_result_path(runtime_path, task_id).parent / "runtime"


def write_task_result(runtime_path: Path, result: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Path:
    """Atomically publish the sole persisted task-run result."""
    path = task_result_path(runtime_path, str(result["task_id"]))
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".result.", suffix=".tmp", dir=path.parent)
    temp_path = Path(temp_name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(dict(result), handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            handle.write("\n")
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(temp_path, path)
    finally:
        temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return path


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    """Wall-clock stamp for the receipt; the runtime's own clock, never a test's."""
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z")


def runner_liveness(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Advisory pid check on the runner that wrote this record.

    A lane's record read `timed-out` while its runner was visibly alive (#791),
    and the record could not say which reading was stale because it carried no
    process identity. `alive` is `os.kill(pid, 0)` at read time, never
    persisted, and only advisory: a pid can be reused, and a live runner on a
    terminal record is normal while the runner finishes retention after its
    final write. A `running` record whose pid is dead is the one firm reading:
    that record is stale.
    """
    pid = record.get("runner_pid")
    if isinstance(pid, bool) or not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0:
        return {"runner_pid": None, "alive": None}
    try:
        os.kill(pid, 0)
        alive = True
    except ProcessLookupError:
        alive = False
    except PermissionError:
        alive = True
    except OverflowError:
        alive = None
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno not in {errno.EINVAL, errno.EOVERFLOW}:
            raise
        alive = None
    return {"runner_pid": pid, "alive": alive}


def read_task_result(runtime_path: Path, task_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    path = task_result_path(runtime_path, task_id)
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise TaskRunError(f"task result must be a JSON object: {path}")
    return payload


def read_task_results(runtime_path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    root = runtime_path / "task-run"
    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for path in sorted(root.glob("*/result.json")) if root.is_dir() else []:
        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise TaskRunError(f"task result must be a JSON object: {path}")
        results.append(payload)
    return results


def task_status(repo_root: Path, task_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read this repo's task-run result store without mutation."""
    resolved_repo = _git_owner._require_git_root(repo_root)
    runtime_path = task_runtime_root(resolved_repo)
    if task_id is not None:
        record = read_task_result(runtime_path, task_id)
        if record is not None:
            return {**record, "liveness": runner_liveness(record)}
        return {
            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
            "event": "task-status",
            "repo_root": str(resolved_repo),
            "task_id": task_id,
            "status": "missing",
            "result_path": str(task_result_path(runtime_path, task_id)),
        }
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "event": "task-status-list",
        "repo_root": str(resolved_repo),
        "runtime_root": str(runtime_path),
        "tasks": [
            {**record, "liveness": runner_liveness(record)}
            for record in read_task_results(runtime_path)
        ],
    }


def _failure_payload(
    *,
    repo_root: Path | None,

        "worktree_path": str(target_path) if target_path is not None else None,

        "next_step": "Fix the preflight error, then rerun task run from a clean parent with an unused worktree path.",
    }

"""Event bytes survive every way a lane's executor can end, or the loss is recorded.

The carrier stamps executor stdout through a pipe (`StampingPipe`). The
v8.15.0 release critique (R1) found that close() could give up on the reader
and the caller then closed the sink, dropping bytes silently. These pin the
contract: everything written before close reaches the events log
byte-for-byte on normal exit, timeout, a signalled child and a parent
interrupt; a writer that outlives close, or a failing sink, is reported in
the capture receipt and never blocks the executor.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import os
import shutil
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from scripts.task_run import task_run_event_timing as timing
from scripts.task_run import task_run_execution

from .test_task_run_fixtures import _codex, _repo, _run

pytestmark = pytest.mark.boundary_contract(
    reason="the claim is what a real executor process leaves in the pipe on timeout, signal and detach"
)

STAMP = "2026-10-20T08:00:00.000Z"
LINES = (
    b'{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"fake-thread"}\n'
    b'{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"c1","type":"command_execution"}}\n'
    b"plain progress text\n"
)
PARTIAL = b'{"type":"turn'
STAMPED = (
    b'{"charness_received_at":"2026-10-20T08:00:00.000Z","type":"thread.started",'
    b'"thread_id":"fake-thread"}\n'
    b'{"charness_received_at":"2026-10-20T08:00:00.000Z","type":"item.started",'
    b'"item":{"id":"c1","type":"command_execution"}}\n'
    b"plain progress text\n"
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _fixed_clock(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "utc_receive_stamp", lambda: STAMP)


def _emit_body(tail: str) -> str:
    # printf %s keeps the bytes exact; the partial line has no newline.
    payload = (LINES + PARTIAL).decode("ascii").replace("'", "'\\''")
    return f"printf 'VALUE = 2\\n' > module.py\nprintf '%s' '{payload}'\n{tail}"


def _events(payload: dict[str, object]) -> bytes:
    """This run's slice of the lane events log (the log appends across runs)."""
    window = payload["execution"]["event_log_window"]  # type: ignore[index]
    with Path(window["path"]).open("rb") as handle:
        handle.seek(window["offset_bytes"])
        return handle.read(window["byte_count"])


def test_timeout_keeps_every_event_byte_including_the_partial_tail(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    executable = _codex(tmp_path, _emit_body("sleep 5"))

    payload = _run(repo, tmp_path, executable, timeout_seconds=1)

    assert payload["status"] == "timed-out"
    # The retained log ends the partial line with the newline retention adds.
    assert _events(payload) == STAMPED + PARTIAL + b"\n"
    assert "event_capture_incomplete" not in payload["execution"]


def test_a_signalled_child_keeps_every_event_byte(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

    payload = _run(repo, tmp_path, executable)

    assert payload["candidate"]["status"] == "wip"

    def writing_then_interrupted(*_args, **_kwargs):

def test_a_writer_that_outlives_close_is_reported_not_waited_on(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "_CLOSE_GRACE_SECONDS", 0.2)
    sink = io.BytesIO()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=lambda: STAMP)
    descendant = os.dup(pipe.fileno())  # a descendant that escaped the group kill
    try:
        os.write(descendant, LINES + PARTIAL)
        pipe.close()
        capture = pipe.capture()
    finally:
        os.close(descendant)

    # Everything written before close is kept; what the survivor writes later
    # is not, and the receipt says so instead of staying silent.
    assert sink.getvalue() == STAMPED + PARTIAL
    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["writer_open_at_close"] is True
    assert capture["received_bytes"] == len(LINES + PARTIAL)


class _FailingSink(io.BytesIO):
    def write(self, data: bytes) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]
        raise OSError(28, "No space left on device")


def test_a_failing_sink_is_reported_and_never_blocks_the_executor() -> None:
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(_FailingSink(), clock=lambda: STAMP)
    # Far more than a pipe buffer: a reader that stopped draining would block
    # this writer forever, which is how a failed sink would hang the lane.
    flood = b'{"type":"item.started"}\n' * 40_000
    writer = threading.Thread(target=os.write, args=(pipe.fileno(), flood), daemon=True)
    writer.start()
    writer.join(timeout=10)
    assert not writer.is_alive()
    pipe.close()

    capture = pipe.capture()
    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["error"] == "OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device"
    assert capture["received_bytes"] == len(flood)
    assert capture["dropped_bytes"] > 0


class _ShortSink(io.BytesIO):
    def write(self, data: bytes) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]
        return super().write(bytes(data)[:-1]) if len(data) > 1 else super().write(data)


def test_a_short_sink_write_is_recorded_as_lost_bytes() -> None:
    """A sink that accepts only part of a line must not leave capture 'complete'
    (release critique follow-up R-002)."""
    sink = _ShortSink()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=lambda: STAMP)
    os.write(pipe.fileno(), b'{"type":"a"}\n{"type":"b"}\n')
    pipe.close()

    capture = pipe.capture()
    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["error"].startswith("short write: ")
    assert capture["dropped_bytes"] > 0


def test_incomplete_capture_reaches_the_execution_record(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    if shutil.which("setsid") is None:
        pytest.skip("setsid is unavailable")
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "_CLOSE_GRACE_SECONDS", 0.2)
    repo = _repo(tmp_path)
    # A detached descendant keeps stdout open past the process-group kill; the
    # executor exits only once it has left the group, so the kill cannot win.
    ready = tmp_path / "detached"
    executable = _codex(
        tmp_path,
        _emit_body(
            f"setsid sh -c 'touch {ready}; exec sleep 3' &\n"
            f"while [ ! -e {ready} ]; do :; done"
        ),
    )

    payload = _run(repo, tmp_path, executable)

    gaps = payload["execution"]["event_capture_incomplete"]
    assert [(gap["invocation"], gap["writer_open_at_close"]) for gap in gaps] == [(0, True)]
    assert _events(payload).startswith(STAMPED + PARTIAL)
    json.dumps(payload)  # the receipt stays serializable


class _HungSink(io.BytesIO):
    """A sink whose first write blocks until the test releases it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.entered = threading.Event()
        self.release = threading.Event()

    def write(self, data: bytes) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]
        self.entered.set()
        self.release.wait(timeout=30)
        return super().write(data)


def test_a_hung_sink_cannot_hang_close_or_receive_writes_after_it(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "_CLOSE_GRACE_SECONDS", 0.05)
    sink = _HungSink()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=lambda: STAMP)
    os.write(pipe.fileno(), LINES)
    assert sink.entered.wait(timeout=30)

    pipe.close()  # returns although the reader is stuck in the sink
    capture = pipe.capture()
    sink.release.set()
    pipe._thread.join(timeout=30)

    assert capture["complete"] is False
    assert capture["error"] == "event reader did not finish before close"
    # The stuck write finishes; every later line is dropped and counted.
    assert pipe.capture()["dropped_bytes"] > 0
    assert sink.getvalue().count(b"\n") == 1


def test_a_failing_clock_keeps_the_bytes_unstamped_and_records_it() -> None:
    def broken_clock() -> str:
        raise ValueError("clock broke")

    sink = io.BytesIO()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=broken_clock)
    os.write(pipe.fileno(), LINES + PARTIAL)
    pipe.close()

    assert sink.getvalue() == LINES + PARTIAL
    assert pipe.capture()["error"] == "ValueError: clock broke"


def test_a_failing_pipe_read_is_recorded(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def failing_select(*_args: object) -> object:
        raise OSError("select failed")

    # Rebinds only the timing module's name, not the process-wide select module.
    monkeypatch.setattr(timing, "select", type("S", (), {"select": staticmethod(failing_select)}))
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(io.BytesIO(), clock=lambda: STAMP)
    pipe.close()

    assert pipe.capture()["error"] == "OSError: select failed"
    assert pipe.capture()["complete"] is False


def test_the_observer_sees_complete_events_and_its_faults_cost_no_bytes() -> None:
    seen: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    def observer(event: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        seen.append(event)
        raise RuntimeError("observer bug")

    sink = io.BytesIO()
    pipe = timing.StampingPipe(sink, clock=lambda: STAMP, observer=observer)
    os.write(pipe.fileno(), LINES + b"{broken json\n" + PARTIAL)
    pipe.close()

    assert sink.getvalue() == STAMPED + b"{broken json\n" + PARTIAL
    # Two JSON objects reach the observer; text, broken JSON and the
    # unfinished line do not, and its exceptions are contained.
    assert [event["type"] for event in seen] == ["thread.started", "item.started"]
    assert pipe.capture()["complete"] is True

JSON line as it arrives on the executor's stdout pipe. Every clock here is
injected; no test reads wall time or waits on a deadline.

def _codex(at: str, kind: str, item: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return json.dumps({FIELD: at, "type": kind, "item": item})


def _muse(at: str, payload_type: str, payload: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    return json.dumps({FIELD: at, "payload_type": payload_type, "payload": payload})

class _Tree:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.state: str | None = "tree-0"

    def __call__(self) -> str | None:
        return self.state


def _rule(window: float = 100.0) -> tuple[rule_owner.ProgressRule, _Tree]:
    tree = _Tree()
    rule = rule_owner.ProgressRule(window_seconds=window, fingerprint=tree)
    rule.start(0.0)
    return rule, tree


def _completed(command: str, item_id: str, exit_code: int = 1) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "type": "item.completed",
        "item": {
            "id": item_id,
            "type": "command_execution",
            "command": command,
            "exit_code": exit_code,
        },
    }
